name: Map Reveal System
description: Fog-of-war for the world map: it decides which rooms the player is allowed to see and tracks how much of each region is known. Its input is trust, not geometry — world.interconnected_map_graph announces which room was entered or first visited, and this component turns those facts into reveal state, because a map that derives 'visited' from raw position can be fooled by clipping, and one that tracks its own graph duplicates the topology. It deliberately does not draw: ui.minimap renders what this marks visible, which keeps cartography policy (what to reveal) separate from cartography rendering (how it looks). For open terrain without rooms it accepts world.vision_system's tile feed as an alternate source of truth, making the same reveal pipeline serve both room-graph and tile-grid worlds. Completion percentage lives here because 'seen' is what this component uniquely knows.

inputs.name: revealMode
inputs.description: room reveals whole rooms on first visit; perimeter reveals only walked areas within a room; region reveals the entire region on first entry, which suits generous handheld-style maps.

inputs.name: showUnvisitedConnections
inputs.description: Whether edges out of visited rooms are drawn before their far end is seen. Showing them advertises 'something is this way' — the genre's primary lure. Hiding them suits mystery-first design.

inputs.name: revealPersistAcrossSessions
inputs.description: Whether reveal state is durable. The actual write is persistence.save_system's job; this flag only declares that the state is worth saving.

outputs.name: completionPercent
outputs.description: Revealed rooms over total rooms. The map-completion figure 100%-runs chase, computed from reveal state because that is the state the player can actually act on.
